summary: The curated contracts and implementations are strongly aligned and fail-closed overall. Two bounded weaknesses remain: framework detection documentation narrows imports to two extensions despite the shared eight-extension contract, and scanner temporary storage trusts an inherited writable TMPDIR instead of creating a private trusted workspace.

findings.title: Framework detection omits six supported extensions
findings.evidence: Phase 0 directs framework-import detection only in `.ts`/`.js` files, while the scanner and generator publicly support `.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.mts`, `.mjs`, `.cts`, and `.cjs` as well. Following this instruction can misclassify supported E2E files and skip framework-specific review checks.
findings.recommendation: Replace the `.ts`/`.js` restriction with the shared eight-extension set used by the scanner and generator.

findings.title: Scanner trusts inherited TMPDIR for security-sensitive state
findings.evidence: Temporary allocation accepts any inherited writable TMPDIR and subsequently stores candidate manifests, findings, and suppression state there. A project-controlled or shared TMPDIR weakens the scanner's otherwise careful path and identity boundary and permits observation or interference by a concurrent process.
findings.recommendation: Create one private mode-0700 scanner workspace beneath a trusted system temporary root, reject project-contained roots, and allocate all temporary files descriptor-relatively within it.

limitations: This packet-only review did not execute scripts, tests, scanners, publishers, downloaders, or verification probes.
Referenced CI helpers, fixtures, manifests, benchmarks, holdouts, reports, and several supporting files were omitted and were not inferred to pass.
This subset review is not full product coverage, skill-accuracy validation, human or sealed review, independent ground truth, or remote model attestation.
